assertions.text: The response identifies at least one statement in the report's profile section as applicable to almost anyone, rather than specific to Elaine.
assertions.evidence: Profile critiques are contradiction/no-evidence, never universality: "Nothing in your paperwork supports it" (natural connector); "no instrument is named" (design thinking). The Barnum lines — "high standards for yourself", "at your best when making a difference", "value authenticity and growth" — go unmentioned.

assertions.text: The response points out that the report's claim that detail and process work drain Elaine is contradicted by her performance reviews or her own intake answers.
assertions.evidence: "§1 The profile is inverted": quotes the report's *"Routine detail and process work drains you"* against intake *"I like building processes and checklists"* and the 2023 review *"Elaine's process documentation is the standard the rest of the site copies."*

assertions.text: The response disputes the report's claim that Elaine can expect UX offers within three to six months of the bootcamp, on grounds of the entry-level UX market or her lack of any design record.
assertions.evidence: §4: quotes "expect offers within three to six months of graduating" then — "No source, no cohort data. The honest picture is harder: UX postings fell sharply after the 2022 peak, entry-level roles draw very large applicant pools, and bootcamp saturation has made the credential itself worth less."

assertions.text: The response states that the report never engages with Elaine's financial situation.
assertions.evidence: Section heading: "3. The money doesn't work, and the report never does the sum" — plus "Their plan does not meet the deadline they were given, on their own numbers, and they never wrote the numbers down" and "No salary figures anywhere... The report never says so."

assertions.text: The response calculates from Elaine's own figures how long her money lasts, or what remains after the £8,900 bootcamp fee.
assertions.evidence: "£26,000 in cash (£19,800 redundancy plus £6,200 savings) against £2,150 a month going out" plus table: "Bootcamp only (£8,900) | £12,800 | around 1 Apr 2027"; "Spend nothing | £21,700 | early Aug 2027".

assertions.text: The response identifies that at least one recommended path conflicts with Elaine's stated twice-weekly care for her mother or her no-nights-away constraint.
assertions.evidence: "Path two puts you on client site *"around four days a week"* in *"London and Manchester."* From Coventry that is either relocation or regular nights away. Both are things you ruled out in writing." Also path three: "aim national... Same collision."

assertions.text: The response criticises the report for ending without recommending or ranking any of the three paths, treating that as a failing rather than a virtue.
assertions.evidence: §6 "There is no wrong choice here": "They cannot all be *'strong matches'* for one person. The one thing you bought, a decision, is the one thing the report declines to make, and *'choose from the heart, you will know'* is advice from a document that got your stated preferences backwards."

assertions.text: The response points out that the report's proposed next steps ask Elaine to spend or commit before any path has been tested.
assertions.evidence: On next step 1: "Don't pay it... The deposit deadline is a sales mechanism." And: "whether you test it with £8,900 and four months of runway, or with £200 and your evenings"; "Test it before you spend, not after."

assertions.text: The response commits to a view on which direction Elaine's record best supports, or proposes a specific better-supported alternative, instead of treating the three paths as equally viable.
assertions.evidence: "My bet, stated plainly so you can hold me to it: the fastest route back to income is your compliance record, sold locally" — plus the specific alternative: "go after interim and contract operations, QA, or compliance work within an hour of Coventry... Pitch... audit readiness."

assertions.text: The response cites at least one specific item from Elaine's work history or performance reviews as contradicting a claim the report makes about her.
assertions.evidence: Against "Routine detail and process work drains you": "Your 2023 review... 'Elaine's process documentation is the standard the rest of the site copies. Her line audit preparation was faultless.'" Also, vs "natural connector": 2025 review "can be short in cross-functional meetings."

assertions.text: The response gives Elaine at least one concrete action for the coming month that costs nothing or nearly nothing.
assertions.evidence: "**Claim new-style JSA this week.** The 182-day clock is better started now." Also free: "**Leave your LinkedIn headline searchable.** Operations manager, BRC, SOPs, continuous improvement" and asking the provider in writing whether the £500 is refundable.

assertions.text: The response advises Elaine not to act on the report as written.
assertions.evidence: "I would not pay the £500 deposit before 5 October." and, under "What I'd do about the 5 October deposit": "**Don't pay it.**" Plus "Leave your LinkedIn headline searchable" against next step 4, and "two of the three paths are unavailable to you".
